title: QBR - PrismCloud - Health Check
next_steps: Send 90-day usage and cost breakdown (Alex) by 2026-04-23
Share upcoming Redwood roadmap items and expected GA dates (Alex) by 2026-04-24
Schedule cost-optimization deep dive with Prism infra team (Priya) for week of 2026-05-04
Run Dedicated capacity benchmark pilot and share results (Priya) by 2026-05-05
action_items: Alex Morgan — Export and send 90-day token-level usage + cost CSV and summary (due 2026-04-23)
Priya Shah — Run latency and throughput baseline for PrismCloud 2k qps scenario and share results (due 2026-05-05)
Sara Li — Provide representative prompt set and 3 production examples for eval (due 2026-04-28)
Daniel Reyes — Confirm budget band and procurement timeline for Dedicated pilot (due 2026-05-01)
header: Date: 2026-04-21 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (PrismCloud CTO), Sara Li (ML Eng), Miguel Torres (Head of Product)
summary: Quarterly business review / health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Discussed cost optimizations (batching, quantization), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, recent outage mitigation and SLOs, and next steps for a Dedicated pilot and shared artifacts.
topics: Usage & Cost trends; Reliability & SLOs; Roadmap & feature ask; Dedicated capacity pilot; Security/compliance questions; Next steps and action items
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our QBR — um, Alex from Redwood here, with Priya, our SE. How's it going?
[00:08] Daniel Reyes: Hey Alex, good to see you. Busy quarter but overall doing well.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya — I'll start with a quick reliability slide and then we can dig into usage.
[00:23] Miguel Torres: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in cost and the Dedicated pilot timeline.
[00:29] Alex Morgan: Great, that's on the agenda. Quick housekeeping: we'll share the 90-day token-level CSV and a summary after the call.
[00:36] Sara Li: Perfect. We'll need the prompt-level breakdown too if possible — that helps our evals.
[00:42] Priya Shah: Yep we can include prompt buckets, approximate token counts, and top endpoints.
[00:51] Alex Morgan: Ok jumping in — usage trend: PrismCloud saw steady growth, about a 28% increase in tokens month-over-month, biggest spike around early March tied to search feature rollout.
[01:05] Daniel Reyes: That matches our internal numbers. Cost seemed higher than expected in March — any visibility?
[01:12] Priya Shah: Looking at the breakdown, 65% of cost was from high-latency generative flows with long context lengths, and about 18% from retries due to 5xx errors which we've been addressing.
[01:23] Miguel Torres: Retries — is that on Redwood or our infra?
[01:29] Priya Shah: Mostly on the application side, some transient timeouts hit the gateway; we rolled a fix mid-March. We've seen error-rate drop from 2.4% to 0.6% since.
[01:41] Sara Li: Good, that explains some savings but we still have high per-token latency on a few endpoints.
[01:47] Alex Morgan: For latency, we've got two levers: Dedicated capacity for pinned low-latency, and batching/quantization changes for hosted tiers. We recommended per-route batching configs last quarter; have you applied those?
[02:00] Daniel Reyes: We applied them to two top routes but not the long-context flows.
[02:06] Priya Shah: That's the low-hanging fruit — batching reduces cost per token but can add ms of latency if you have strict tail SLOs. We can tune batch size and max wait to balance.
[02:19] Miguel Torres: Can Redwood show us a simulation of cost vs median/tail latency if we change batching from 20ms to 50ms?
[02:27] Priya Shah: Yes — I'll run a simulation and add it to the benchmark doc. Expect a ~12-18% cost reduction for those routes with a small 10-20ms median increase.
[02:39] Alex Morgan: On quantization — switching to 4-bit for some non-critical models reduced costs for a different customer by ~30% with imperceptible quality loss. Might be worth testing.
[02:51] Sara Li: We need to validate on our prompts; some hallucination-sensitive flows can't afford degraded quality.
[02:57] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll set up an eval with your prompt set — that was listed as an action item.
[03:05] Alex Morgan: Reliability — quick update: there was a 2-hour partial degradation in Feb due to a scheduler bug. Post-mortem is in the incident doc, and mitigations were deployed.
[03:17] Daniel Reyes: Yes we saw increased latencies then. Are there SLA credits or amends?
[03:23] Alex Morgan: For Dedicated customers we have SLA credits; for hosted customers we evaluate on a case-by-case. We'll include the incident summary and proposed credits in the follow-up.
[03:33] Miguel Torres: What about regional failover? We want better multi-region fallback for EU users.
[03:40] Priya Shah: We can route by region with automatic fallback to the nearest compatible model. For PrismCloud we can add a region policy to prefer eu-west while allowing fallback to us-west in emergencies.
[03:52] Sara Li: Any data residency concerns? We need to prove logs and storage remain inside EU for certain datasets.
[03:58] Alex Morgan: For Private deployments or VPC-hosted storage we can guarantee data residency; for hosted we have region-specific storage and can provide audit logs and KMS key control as needed. We'll share the security docs.
[04:12] Daniel Reyes: Talk to me about Dedicated pilot — what's the timeline and what does Redwood need from us?
[04:18] Priya Shah: Pilot would be 2-4 weeks: baseline tests on your workload (we'll run throughput and latency tests), then a short tuning window. We need sample prompt set, expected qps profile, and a contact for infra/networking.
[04:30] Alex Morgan: Also alignment on success criteria: cost per 1k tokens target, p95 latency target, and max error rate.
[04:38] Miguel Torres: We're aiming for p95 < 220ms and error rate < 0.5% for the critical route. Cost target TBD after baseline.
[04:47] Priya Shah: That p95 is doable with Dedicated and correct instance types plus KV cache warmups. We'll include warmup scripts in the repo.
[04:57] Sara Li: What's KV cache? I sometimes see it as K V — caching of prefix keys?
[05:02] Priya Shah: Yes it's KV cache — it holds past keys/values to speed autoregressive generation for longer contexts. Proper cache warming reduces latency significantly.
[05:12] Alex Morgan: Security/compliance check — you asked about SOC 2 and SSO. We have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC controls, integration with customer KMS, and audit logs. Any specific questions?
[05:25] Daniel Reyes: We need the SOC 2 report and SAML metadata for our IdP team. Also want a statement on encryption at rest for embeddings data.
[05:33] Alex Morgan: We'll share SOC2 and the KMS/export docs. Embeddings at rest can be encrypted under your KMS key in Private/Dedicated; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can present options.
[05:45] Miguel Torres: Are there any limits for compute or concurrency in Dedicated?
[05:50] Priya Shah: Dedicated is configurable; you get a pool of GPUs and predictable throughput, plus autoscaling policies. We'll propose instance sizing during the pilot.
[05:59] Alex Morgan: Ok moving to roadmap alignment — upcoming features that may help: better per-route caching controls, cost-aware routing, and token-level billing export improvements.
[06:10] Sara Li: Cost-aware routing is interesting — would let us push low-value traffic to cheaper models.
[06:15] Priya Shah: Exactly — route by policy: latency, cost, or quality. We can configure rules per route.
[06:22] Miguel Torres: Can Redwood support model pinning for audits and reproducibility?
[06:27] Alex Morgan: Yes — model version pinning and rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) are supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted customers get versioning too.
[06:36] Daniel Reyes: On billing, can you produce a per-feature cost report so our finance team can allocate expenses?
[06:42] Alex Morgan: Yes we can produce per-route and per-team cost allocation exports — will include sample in the data pack.
[06:50] Priya Shah: For the action items recap: Alex will send usage+cost CSV, Priya will run the Dedicated benchmark, and Sara will share the prompt set. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff once budget is confirmed.
[07:02] Miguel Torres: Timeline-wise we want the pilot in early May if procurement goes through in time.
[07:08] Alex Morgan: Noted. We'll plan for a May 4th pilot kickoff window.
[07:12] Daniel Reyes: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:15] Priya Shah: No blockers; we need the sample prompts, an infra contact for networking/VPN, and confirmation of data residency constraints.
[07:24] Sara Li: I'll send prompts and sample payloads by Tuesday.
[07:28] Alex Morgan: Great, and I'll attach the security pack and the incident post-mortem.
[07:34] Miguel Torres: One last Q on cost — do you offer committed usage discounts for Dedicated?
[07:39] Alex Morgan: Yes — reserved capacity contracts with monthly or annual commits. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[07:46] Daniel Reyes: Ok thanks, that helps.
[07:49] Priya Shah: Any final questions?
[07:52] Miguel Torres: None from me.
[07:54] Sara Li: All good.
[07:56] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[08:01] Daniel Reyes: Thanks Alex, Priya — talk soon.
[08:04] Alex Morgan: Bye all.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription noise, occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cache spelled out), and natural speech patterns. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/usage/prismcloud (usage CSV), /s/roadmap (roadmap doc), incident-postmortem-2026-02 (incident doc).
